sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 WebGPURenderer with automatic WebGL2 recovery; Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio; native JavaScript; AI Hub Session Protocol v1. Three.js MIT; Rapier Apache-2.0.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original procedural cel-shaded geometry with ink outlines, layered teal caverns and parchment expedition typography
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip limb tracks, plus procedural creature, balloon and environmental motion
sourceInformation.audio: Code-only adaptive music, synthesized effects and Animalese-style gibberish voices; music defaults to 10%
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 player shared-world co-op through AI Hub, BroadcastChannel local tabs, or manual WebRTC peer connection; host authoritative
sourceInformation.testing: Unrestricted headless testing, scripted full physics playthrough, injected standard gamepad, touch emulation, offline Web Audio PCM, two-page local/WebRTC peers and official AI Hub conformance. No FPS target. Physical controller, real mobile devices and hardware WebGPU unknown.
sourceInformation.research: none; native model knowledge only. The explicitly supplied AI Hub integration code and protocol were read.

testingFeedback: Browser execution exposed five issues: balloon drift, shader warm-up blocking session readiness, environment WebGPU device loss, initial gamepad focus, and touch HUD input detection. Additional review fixed co-op lifecycle and touch/balloon edge cases.
Three blocked route completion, graphics, or session readiness before correction. The graphics failure also reproduces in a minimal native WebGPU page; automatic WebGL2 recovery handles it.
The complete actual-physics expedition, plus the official two-player and dedicated-server AI Hub harness.
The first WebGPU screenshot: its blank canvas could not distinguish an environment failure from a scene bug. The minimal GPU probe and compatibility-backend rendering were more useful.
engineFeedback: Three.js native node materials and AnimationMixer make the cel-shaded scene and character animation fit together cleanly.
Integration assumptions around collision openings, ladder exits and the session lifecycle needed browser verification.
The complete exploration controller, cavern layout, procedural art, audio, menus and authoritative co-op simulation.
Coordinating Rapier kinematic movement with ladders, water and balloon attachment without breaking world collision.
A built-in inspectable character-controller layer for swimming, ladders and moving attachments would reduce integration work.
promptFeedback: The source, single-file delivery and controller-first requirements give the demo a clear creative and practical target.
The no-internet research rule sits beside a required online protocol link; I treated that link as integration documentation, with no creative research.
Making a complete connected cavern route and checking both its movement mechanics and multiplayer lifecycle in headless browsers.
Separate mandatory acceptance checks from creative preferences, and state the desired approximate playtime.

aiHub.name: Pitfall-ish - The Understory
aiHub.tagline: Some treasures have legs. Best bring them home.
aiHub.description: Descend into an ink-lined cavern to reunite a lost expedition. Jump, climb, swim and hitch a balloon ride home, alone or with a fellow explorer.
aiHub.controls: Stick / WASD: move, climb and swim; Cross / Space: jump or dismount; Square / E: catch balloon; Triangle / M: map; Options / Esc: pause. Touch: drag left, tap right.
